given_when_then.given: A Store Partner updates the quantity of a perishable SKU in their Real-Time Inventory Snapshot
given_when_then.when: The Order Allocation Engine attempts to allocate an Order Request for that SKU
given_when_then.then: The system shall reflect the updated quantity immediately and allow allocation only if stock is sufficient

given_when_then.given: An Order Request has successfully locked stock for a perishable item
given_when_then.when: The customer cancels the Order Request before the fulfillment task begins
given_when_then.then: The system shall release the locked stock quantity back to the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot for other orders

given_when_then.given: The Order Allocation Engine attempts to allocate stock for an Order Request
given_when_then.when: The allocation occurs immediately upon request confirmation
given_when_then.then: The system shall lock the available stock quantities exclusively to prevent concurrent overselling

given_when_then.given: An Order Request is not confirmed within the allocated time window
given_when_then.then: The system shall automatically release the locked stock quantity back to the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot

given_when_then.given: The Order Allocation Engine detects a synchronization discrepancy
given_when_then.when: The data link latency exceeds the defined threshold or a sync failure is detected
given_when_then.then: The system shall flag the synchronization discrepancy for review by the Platform Operator

success_criteria: Stock quantities are locked exclusively to a single Order Request until the fulfillment task is completed or the order is cancelled.
Perishable items are prioritized for allocation to orders based on their proximity to the expiration date.
Synchronization discrepancies are flagged when the data link latency exceeds the defined threshold or if a sync failure is detected.
Locked stock is automatically released if the Order Request is not confirmed within the allocated time window.
Real-Time Inventory Snapshot reflects stock updates immediately upon allocation attempts.
